headline: NEM +4.2%, BARRICK +4.2%, GOLD FIELDS +5.7%: U.S. GOLD AND SILVER MINERS SURGE ON IRAN DEAL OPTIMISM
snippet: U.S. gold and silver mining stocks surged on June 12 as growing optimism over an imminent US-Iran peace deal reduced fears of persistent inflation and further rate hikes — Newmont rose 4.2%, Barrick Mining gained 4.2%, Gold Fields surged 5.7%, Coeur Mining climbed 5.5%, Hecla Mining advanced 3.7%, and Endeavour Silver increased 6.2%, with gold trading near $4,200/oz and silver above $67 after their largest single-session recoveries in weeks. The catalyst was Trump's reversal on scheduled Iran strikes, with the president stating that discussions and final points on a peace deal had been approved by all parties involved — removing the dual headwind that has suppressed precious metals since early May: war-driven inflation expectations lifting rate-hike odds, and the dollar's geopolitical safe-haven premium competing directly with gold.

headline: SOUTHERN CROSS GOLD: 36.6m AT 6.5 g/t AuEq, TWO NEW HIGH-GRADE ZONES UNCOVERED AT APOLLO EAST — 11 RIGS, 200,000m CAMPAIGN
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated Ltd (TSX: SXGC / ASX: SX2) released June 10 drill results from seven holes at the Apollo and Apollo East prospects within its Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria, Australia — standout intercept SDDSC202 returned 36.6 metres at 6.5 g/t AuEq (4.0 g/t Au, 1.0% Sb) from 700 metres depth with individual assays up to 493 g/t Au and 29.1% Sb, while SDDSC214W1 extended Apollo East 20 metres eastward with 0.5 metres at 251.4 g/t AuEq, and step-out SDDSC217 delivered the shallowest Apollo East results to date at 325 metres depth confirming high antimony tenor near surface. The project now holds 96 composite intersections exceeding 100 g/t·m AuEq, with 11 drill rigs advancing the 200,000-metre program through Q1 2027 — making Sunday Creek one of the most active high-grade gold-antimony drill programs in the southern hemisphere.

headline: ALL THREE OGDEN HOLES HIT VISIBLE GOLD IN TIMMINS — Metals Creek Wraps 2026 Program, Assays Ship to Actlab
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Metals Creek Resources
snippet: Metals Creek Resources Corp. (TSXV: MEK) announced June 11 that all three holes in its 2026 drill program at the Ogden Gold Project in Timmins, Ontario — a 50/50 joint venture operated by Metals Creek with Discovery Silver — intersected visible gold, including hole TOG-26-77 cutting visible gold at 350.36 metres depth within strongly altered felsite near the Thomas Ogden Zone fold axis. The 2026 program is now complete and all half-core samples have been shipped to Actlab for gold-silver fire assay; assay results will be released as received. Historic drilling at Ogden has returned intercepts up to 210 g/t Au over 12.5 metres, setting meaningful expectations for the Abitibi gold camp's investor community as it waits for hard numbers from an area where every gram-metre of gold in proximity to Timmins infrastructure commands attention.

headline: CANADA BACKS E3 LITHIUM WITH $36.5M: Clearwater DLE Feasibility Study Fully Funded in Alberta Brine Play
snippet: E3 Lithium Ltd. (TSXV: ETL) announced June 10 the execution of a contribution agreement with Natural Resources Canada confirming up to $36.5 million in non-repayable federal funding to complete Phase 3 of its Clearwater Project Demonstration Facility and a bankable Feasibility Study — covering 75% of the approximately $48 million program, retroactive to April 1, 2026. The funding supports operation of E3's 30-column Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) system already commissioned and construction of a commercial-scale single DLE column at its Alberta oil sands region brine project — a technology that avoids the evaporation-pond footprint and community opposition hampering South American lithium development, positioning Clearwater as a potential anchor of a Canadian domestic lithium supply chain at a time when lithium carbonate above $24,000/tonne has returned commercial viability to Western brine and hard-rock producers.

headline: METALS FOCUS 2026: "BULL RUN RESUMES IN H2" — Dollar, Fiscal, Central Bank Demand All Intact After War Selloff
snippet: Metals Focus's Gold Focus 2026 report, republished on GoldSeek, maintains a bullish second-half 2026 forecast despite gold's 27% correction from the January $5,589 peak to the current $4,100-4,200 range, arguing that every structural driver that pushed gold to record highs — U.S. fiscal trajectory, dollar debasement concerns, stretched equity valuations, elevated geopolitical risk, and persistent central bank accumulation — remains fully intact. Analysts expect the bull run to resume once war uncertainty resolves, identifying the Hormuz agreement and the June 16-17 Warsh FOMC dot plot as the two sequential catalysts that would unlock the paper-market short covering required to drive gold back toward the $5,500-6,000 institutional cluster; for junior mining investors, the implication is that producers currently trading at decade-low P/E multiples against record cash flow per ounce are mispriced in a way that resolves sharply when sentiment shifts.

headline: WARSH'S TRIMMED PCE UNDERSTATES INFLATION EVEN MORE THAN POWELL DID — Money Metals Flags Hidden Gold Catalyst for FOMC Week
snippet: A June 9 analysis by Mike Maharrey of Money Metals Exchange, republished on GoldSeek, argues that Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's stated preference for trimmed mean PCE inflation measurement would structurally understate consumer price pressures even more than the core PCE already does — because the trim removes the fastest-rising components (currently energy and food, the exact inputs that Iran-conflict supply disruptions are driving highest) and creates an official inflation narrative that diverges from lived purchasing-power experience. The paradoxical gold implication: if Warsh anchors his June 16-17 press conference on trimmed PCE, the official rate path will appear less aggressive than the actual inflation environment warrants, widening the gap between official and experienced inflation — a condition that historically accelerates physical precious metals accumulation by investors who distrust headline CPI numbers as a reflection of their real cost of living.

headline: HOW NEM, BARRICK, AGNICO, KINROSS NAVIGATE THE PULLBACK: MARGINS HOLD BUT CAPITAL RETURN EXPECTATIONS PRESSURE PRODUCERS
snippet: Kalkine Media's June 10 analysis examines how gold's multi-week correction from $5,589 to the $4,100-4,200 range is testing the capital return discipline and margin commitments of the four largest gold producers — Newmont (NEM), Barrick Mining (ABX), Agnico Eagle (AEM), and Kinross Gold (KGC) — noting that all four remain highly profitable at current gold prices but face simultaneous pressure from rising all-in sustaining costs, shareholder expectations for buybacks and dividends established during the $5,000+ gold environment, and the strategic need to invest in organic reserve replacement. For self-directed investors choosing between majors and juniors during the pullback, the analysis frames the core question as whether to pay for proven production with tight capital allocation or buy juniors at maximum leverage to the eventual recovery — a calculus that resolves differently depending on the investor's time horizon and risk tolerance.

headline: SPROTT: 28 GW OF AI-LINKED NUCLEAR CAPACITY ANNOUNCED AS URANIUM HOLDS $86/LB — June Miners Surge on Inflows
snippet: Sprott's June 11 uranium market update shows spot prices holding at $86.1/lb globally (¥583/lb in China) in a cautious holding pattern as utilities draw on working inventories and limit near-term spot purchases — while the structural demand picture strengthens materially, with Sprott counting over 28 gigawatts of announced nuclear capacity tied specifically to AI data centres and digital infrastructure, a new price-insensitive long-cycle demand vector that did not exist in the last uranium bull cycle. Uranium miners surged in June supported by renewed institutional inflows as the supply-side case tightens: mines are operating near full capacity and the undeveloped deposit universe requires $100+/lb uranium to reach investment decision economics. With utility term contracting expected to resume in H2 2026, the current consolidation below $90/lb may represent the final accumulation window before the next contract-driven buying wave.

headline: BIRCH GOLD: AN IRAN DEAL PUTS GOLD BACK ON TRACK — But Warsh Must Also Frame Inflation as Supply Shock at June 16-17 FOMC
snippet: Birch Gold's analysis, published as gold rebounds from its June correction to the $4,200 range, argues that a confirmed US-Iran deal is a necessary but not sufficient condition for gold to resume its structural bull market path toward the $5,500-6,000 institutional targets — because the correction was driven by two overlapping forces (war-driven inflation expectations raising rate-hike odds, AND the USD safe-haven bid competing with gold), and a peace deal removes both simultaneously. The deeper argument: the FOMC meeting on June 16-17 is the second required catalyst — a Warsh dot plot that frames current inflation as supply-shock-driven rather than demand-driven would signal the rate hike cycle is near its peak, removing the real-yield headwind that accounts for most of the remaining gap between current spot and institutional year-end targets. For investors who built positions during the June dip, the analysis frames the next two weeks as a potential sequential unlocking of two suppressive forces rather than a simple mean reversion.

headline: MOGOTES METALS +159% THIS WEEK: 3,681m OF FILO SUR ASSAYS DUE IN JUNE — Albor Already Shows 86m AT 0.7% Cu
snippet: Mogotes Metals Inc. (TSXV: MOG) surged 159% during the most recent trading week to a market cap of approximately C$287 million, driven by investor anticipation of assay results from 3,681 metres of unannounced drilling at the Filo Sur Project in Argentina's Vicuña district — expected in June from the Luz del Sol and Meseta target cluster. The company has already confirmed two high-grade discoveries in the same season: the Cruz del Sur shallow gold breccia underlain by a copper-gold-molybdenum porphyry (120 metres at 0.52 g/t Au) and the Albor porphyry (86 metres at 0.7% Cu, 0.55 g/t Au, 2.7 g/t Ag from just 108 metres depth including 43 metres at 1.1% Cu), drilled immediately along strike from BHP and Lundin Mining's world-class Filo del Sol deposit. With June being the anticipated window for the Luz del Sol cluster results, the 159% weekly gain prices in a potential third porphyry discovery in the Americas' hottest copper-gold exploration district.
